# Vulnerabilities this project knowingly ships with.
#
# The dependency audit fails the build on anything not listed here. That is
# the point: an audit that cannot fail is an audit nobody reads, and the
# previous version of this job ended in `|| echo warning`, which meant the
# green tick said nothing about whether the dependencies were safe.
#
# But a job that fails on every newly-published advisory, including ones with
# no released fix, gets switched off within a fortnight. So there is a way to
# accept one — in writing, with a reason, and with a date on which somebody
# has to look again. An entry whose review date has passed FAILS the build,
# which is what stops this file from quietly becoming the `|| true` it
# replaced.
#
# Format, whitespace-separated:
#
#   <advisory-id>  <review-by YYYY-MM-DD>  <why this is acceptable>
#
# The advisory id is whatever the tool prints — GHSA-…, PYSEC-…, CVE-…, or an
# npm numeric id. Before adding one, answer the question it raises: is the
# vulnerable code path reachable from this application at all? Say so in the
# reason. "Transitive dependency" is not a reason; "parser is only reached
# for files this application never reads" is.
#
# Empty at the time of writing: every known advisory in both dependency trees
# has a fix released, and this project has taken it.
